title: Resiliency standup briefing — Feb 14 2027
content:
Purpose: quick weekly briefing for the SRE team covering incidents, SLO posture, runbook changes, and the on-call handoff notes. This is a working doc — notes, action items, and open questions are inlined.

TL;DR:
- Major incident on 2027-02-12 (partial degradation of hotspot routing) caused 1.7h elevated tail latency for hosted-api region-us-east. Auto-fallback prevented customer-visible failures but latency exceeded SLO for 2 dependent routes.
- SLO status: overall token-generation availability 99.92% (target 99.95%) for the week — borderline but within escalation threshold. Tail-latency SLOs (p95/p99) trended up during peak hours; root causes identified (routing churn + kernel eviction).
- Runbook updates drafted for routing-fallback and cache-warmup (see linked PR).
- On-call handoff notes: Marcus covers Feb 14–20 primary; Diego shadow for database/cache escalations.

1) Incident recap: INC-2027-02-12-1 (routing hotspot & kernel eviction)
- Timeline summary:
  - 02/12 03:12 UTC: First alerts for elevated p99 latency on hosted-api-prod-route/generate-text-us-east.
  - 02/12 03:15 UTC: Auto-fallback to variant-b invoked; requests started using variant with slightly higher cost but lower latency.
  - 02/12 03:25–04:45 UTC: Periodic spikes as routing table churned due to node rebalancing and ephemeral kernel OOM evictions on two GPU hosts.
  - 02/12 05:00 UTC: Stabilized after rolling-restart of one node group and applying conservative packing limits.
- Impact: p99 latency exceeded 2x target for ~1.7 hours; estimated customer-visible degraded latency on 3 premium customers (CS outreach initiated). No data loss or failed requests (fallback worked).
- Root cause hypothesis: simultaneous autoscaler-driven instance spin-up + a recent optimized-attention kernel (PR #827) has a memory regression on certain hardware/driver combos causing kernel eviction under specific sequence lengths.
- Evidence: kernel OOM logs on gpu-host-07 and gpu-host-12; correlating traffic histograms showed sudden burst of long-context requests from demo-workload.
- Temporary mitigations applied: pinned older kernel variant for affected pool, raised eviction threshold, added packing limit to node pool config.
- Next steps / action items (owners):
  - (Diego) Reproduce locally with driver 525.x and long-context inputs; open formal bug if reproduces (JIRA-RW-1345).
  - (Marcus) Patch orchestration to stagger autoscaler ramp-ups during known release windows (small change roll out this week).
  - (Aisha) Notify product/CS with timeline + customer impact summary (done 02/13).
  - (Rina) Add dedicated alert for kernel-oom patterns (monitor rule draft: kernel_oom_count > 0 for 3m) — target 02/16.

2) SLO posture this week
- Metrics snapshot (rolling 7d):
  - Token-gen availability: 99.92% (target 99.95%)
  - p95 latency (text-generation, us-east): 210ms (target 200ms)
  - p99 latency: 1.2s (target 700ms) — spikes driven by routing churn windows; baseline outside of incidents is within targets.
- Actions:
  - Investigate routing-level throttling thresholds — draft change to reduce burst window from 60s -> 30s for high-priority routes (RFC 02/17).
  - Run an A/B test of the new packing limits on a smaller pool to validate impact on p99.

3) Runbook & playbook updates
- Summary of proposed edits (see PR link):
  - Add explicit steps for 'kernel OOM' detection and fallback flow (include exact kubectl/journalctl grep commands, patch rollback checklist).
  - Add guidance for 'staggered autoscaling' and how to apply emergency rate-limits at the LB layer.
  - Cache-warmup playbook: when bringing a new node pool online, pre-warm KV-prefix cache using sample traces to avoid first-request penalties.
- Status: draft PR opened against runbooks repo (GH PR 827); reviewers: Rina, Marcus. Target merge by 02/17.

4) On-call handoffs & rotations
- Current rotation notes:
  - Outgoing: Aisha (primary) — handed off active items and list of open tickets to Marcus.
  - Incoming primary: Marcus Li (02/14–02/20). Shadow: Diego Alvarez (database/cache).
  - Escalation contacts: Rina Matsuo (L2 kernel/infra), Priya Sharma (SRE manager).
- Handoff checklist (short):
  - Confirm alt-runbook links are accessible from jump-host.
  - Share recent incident triage notes + list of risky nodes/pools.
  - Ensure pager rotations in PagerDuty reflect current on-call (checked 02/14 09:10 PST).

5) Capacity & planned maintenance
- Planned: rolling OS/driver update for gpu-host pool-3 on 02/18 00:00–04:00 UTC. Expected brief latency blips during node reboots.
- Mitigation: move traffic off one AZ at a time, enabling graceful draining; pre-warm cache as per new playbook.
- Risk: driver update might interact with kernel variants — staging test on 02/16.

6) Open risks & questions
- Are there customer traffic patterns that require dynamic packing limits (per-customer)? (ACTION: Product + Solutions to weigh in by 02/21).
- Should we temporarily increase default fallback pool capacity for peak windows? (ACTION: Marcus to propose conservative bump config).

7) Quick wins / low-effort items
- Add synthetic load test targeted at long-context request shapes to CI job (Diego, backlog RW-1378).
- Extend p99 alert window to include upstream kernel_oom metric (Rina).

8) Notes to self / brain-dump (informal)
- We keep chasing p99 with band-aids; long-term we need better admission control at API layer for long-context heavy requests. Short-term trick is smart routing + pre-warm.
- Customer outreach script exists in CS playbook but add an optional apology note for latency-sensitive customers.

Appendix: links & references\- Incident timeline (timeline + logs): https://confluence.redwood.com/display/SRE/incident-INC-2027-02-12-1\- Runbook PR: github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/827\- Related jira: JIRA-RW-1345

Action item tracker (short):
- RW-1345 (Diego) reproduce & file upstream bug — due 02/18.
- Runbook PR review (Rina/Marcus) — due 02/17.
- Alert for kernel_oom (Rina) — due 02/16.
- Autoscaler stagger change (Marcus) — deploy canary 02/17.

If anything missing or if you want deeper dig into the kernel logs I pulled, ping me in #sre-ops or DM.

-- Aisha
